knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly explains how a GLM joins exponential-family response, linear predictor eta, and link g(mu)=eta while distinguishing eta from the link?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the structure discrimination for the link LO.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Link competence requires naming response family, eta, and g(mu)=eta as distinct structural pieces.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Exponential-family response; eta = X beta; g(mu)=eta; link is not eta.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Conflating the link with the linear predictor or skipping the three-part join.

choices.label: The response is in an exponential family; eta = X beta is the linear predictor; g(mu) = eta links the mean to that predictor. The link function is not the same object as eta.
Eta and the link are the same object, so writing g(mu) = eta is only optional notation.
The link replaces the exponential-family response, and eta is unused once a family is named.
GLMs join only a Normal response to an identity mean with no separate link idea.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names a non-Normal family with its canonical link and justifies the choice from mean range?
knowledge_checks.body: Choose distributional link warrant; refuse software-default theatre.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Canonical links are justified by mean range and support, not by software defaults.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson-log or binomial-logit with mean-range justification.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting a software-default justification without mean-range reasoning.

choices.label: Poisson with log (canonical): mean is positive and log maps (0, infinity) to the reals for eta. Binomial with logit is similarly justified by mapping probabilities in (0,1) to the real line.
Any link is canonical for any family because software will pick a default automatically.
Poisson with logit as canonical because counts are probabilities on (0,1).
Binomial with identity as canonical because probabilities already equal eta with no transform needed for mean range.

worked_example.title: Logit and log canonical links with numeric η
worked_example.problem_statement:
A GLM uses a link g so that η = g(μ) = xᵀβ.
(a) For a binomial probability μ = 0.25, compute the canonical logit link η = ln(μ/(1 − μ)).
(b) For a Poisson mean with linear predictor η = 1.2, compute μ = e^η.
State the canonical links for binomial and Poisson.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compute logit(0.25) and e^{1.2} before naming canonical links.

steps.label: Canonical logit at μ = 0.25
steps.explanation: The binomial canonical link is the logit.

steps.label: Poisson mean from η = 1.2
steps.attempt_cue: Invert the log link: μ = e^η.
steps.explanation: The Poisson canonical link is the log, so the mean is the exponential of the linear predictor.

steps.label: Name canonical links
steps.attempt_cue: State canonical g for binomial and Poisson.
steps.explanation: Canonical links maximise the correspondence between natural parameter and linear predictor.

worked_example.final_answer: logit(0.25) ≈ −1.0986; Poisson μ = e^{1.2} ≈ 3.3201. Canonical links: logit (binomial), log (Poisson).
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using the identity link as if it were canonical for Poisson, or confusing logit with log.
